developer: Constructor injection with `final` fields; no field `@Autowired`. Check bean scope and qualifiers before adding a bean.
Controllers validate and map; services hold logic; repositories hold queries. Return DTOs, not entities.
Parameterized queries only. Transactions belong on service methods with the right propagation and read-only flags.
Handle errors through the shared exception handler; never swallow an exception.
The impact lookup shows `injected-by` and route couplings: a changed service signature affects every class that injects it.
tester: JUnit tests mirror the package of the class under test; use `@WebMvcTest`/`@DataJpaTest` slices before full `@SpringBootTest`.
Mock collaborators with Mockito at the unit level; assert behaviour and interactions, not private state.
Cover validation failures, not-found and conflict paths of each endpoint, and transactional rollbacks.
Check tests do not depend on test order, system time or a shared database state.
security: No SQL built by concatenation; check JPQL and native queries.
Unsafe deserialization (`ObjectInputStream`, default typing), XXE-prone XML parsers, and `Class.forName` on input.
CSRF, CORS and method security: new endpoints need authorization annotations or config; check `permitAll` additions.
Secrets in `application*.properties` or `.yml` must come from the environment or a vault, not the file.
Dependency changes in `pom.xml` or `build.gradle`: known-vulnerable versions, new transitive repositories.
peer-review: Entity changes need a migration; check Flyway/Liquibase scripts and nullability.
N+1 queries, missing indexes, unbounded `findAll`, lazy loading outside a transaction.
Public API shape changes (JSON fields, status codes) are breaking for clients.
Reflection and Spring wiring by name can hide callers from the graph: search the config for the bean name.
auditor: Rules for Java should mention constructor injection and layering consistently; test-location rules should say `src/test/java` mirroring packages.
